docs.title: Ferry timetable
docs.summary: Departure times for the island ferry.

sections.heading: Weekdays
sections.text: The island ferry leaves the north pier at 07:15 and 17:40.

sections.heading: Weekends
sections.text: On weekends the ferry runs once, leaving at 10:00 from the south pier.

docs.title: Ferry breakdown procedure
docs.summary: What to do when the ferry stops mid crossing.

sections.heading: First steps
sections.text: The skipper radios the harbor office on channel 12.

sections.heading: Passengers
sections.text: The purser hands out blankets and logs the incident in the breakdown ledger.

sections.heading: Visitors
sections.text: Visiting boats pay 18 credits per night at the guest dock.

sections.heading: Members
sections.text: Members moor free for seven nights a year, then pay 6 credits.

docs.title: Net mending guide
docs.summary: How the cooperative repairs fishing nets.

sections.heading: Tools
sections.text: A netting needle and tarred twine are kept in the loft above the smokehouse.

sections.heading: Schedule
sections.text: Mending happens every Thursday morning.

sections.heading: Fire
sections.text: Keep the alder chips away from the flue. A sand bucket hangs by the door.

sections.heading: Hours
sections.text: The smokehouse is closed after dusk.

docs.title: Tide tables
docs.summary: Where the tide charts are posted.

sections.heading: Posting
sections.text: The tide chart is pinned to the harbor office door each Monday.

sections.heading: Spring tides
sections.text: Spring tides flood the lower slipway and the boat lift stays locked.

docs.title: Boat lift operation
docs.summary: Rules for lifting boats out of the water.

sections.heading: Booking
sections.text: Book the boat lift with the yard foreman two days ahead.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: The lift carries a maximum of eight tonnes.

sections.heading: Amounts
sections.text: Full members pay 120 credits each January. Apprentices pay 40 credits.

sections.heading: Late payment
sections.text: Dues unpaid by March lose their vote at the spring assembly.

sections.heading: Agenda
sections.text: The assembly elects the treasurer and approves the season budget.

sections.heading: Voting
sections.text: Each member with paid dues has one vote; proxies are not allowed.

sections.heading: Daily price
sections.text: The quay clerk posts the cod price every morning at six.

sections.heading: Quality grades
sections.text: Grade A fish must be iced within one hour of landing.

sections.heading: Service
sections.text: The ice plant compressor is serviced every March by the refrigeration contractor.

sections.heading: Faults
sections.text: If the ice plant trips, reset the breaker in the cold store, never the pump room.

sections.heading: Shifts
sections.text: Volunteers cover the harbor office from 09:00 to 13:00 on Saturdays.

sections.heading: Swaps
sections.text: Swap shifts by writing on the whiteboard in the net loft.

sections.heading: Found items
sections.text: Found items go into the blue crate in the harbor office for thirty days.

sections.heading: Unclaimed
sections.text: Unclaimed items are given to the charity shop in the village.

sections.heading: Hours
sections.text: The fuel dock sells diesel from 08:00 to 16:00.

sections.heading: Payment
sections.text: Pay by credit card at the pump; no cash is taken on the pier.

docs.title: Storm warning plan
docs.summary: Steps when a gale is forecast.

sections.heading: Signals
sections.text: A red flag on the signal mast means a gale warning; all small boats return.

sections.heading: Moorings
sections.text: Double the mooring lines on the guest dock when the red flag flies.

sections.heading: Duration
sections.text: Apprentices train for two seasons under a named mentor.

sections.heading: Assessment
sections.text: The mentor signs off knots, navigation and net mending before the apprentice becomes a full member.
